facts.text: The hotel is in Lisbon's historic center, between Chiado and Bairro Alto.
facts.excerpt: Bairro Alto Hotel is located in the historic center of Lisbon in a prestigious and emblematic area, made even more special by the several Lisbon sights it offers: it is located between the elegant and cosmopolitan Chiado and the bohemian Bairro Alto.

facts.text: Praca Luis de Camoes is visible from the hotel's entrance.
facts.excerpt: From the entrance of the hotel we see Praça Luís de Camões, which imposes itself as a separation between this neighborhood and Chiado.

facts.text: The hotel is housed in an 18th-century building with a primrose yellow exterior on Praca Luis de Camoes.
facts.excerpt: The distinctive, primrose yellow exterior of the 18th-century building that houses the Bairro Alto Hotel has an impressive perch on the edge of Chiado’s landmark square, the Praça Luís de Camões

facts.text: The hotel first opened in 2005.
facts.excerpt: First opened in 2005, before Lisbon became one of Europe’s hot spots

facts.text: The hotel reopened in 2019 after a three-year renovation.
facts.excerpt: It reopened in 2019 following a three-year renovation.

facts.text: Pritzker Prize winner Eduardo Souto de Moura was part of the team for the renovation.
facts.excerpt: The original team reunited for the re-boot, which included the Pritzker Prize winner, Eduardo Souto de Moura

facts.text: The hotel spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.
facts.excerpt: The hotel is larger and now spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.

facts.text: The interiors include specially commissioned pieces by Portuguese artists such as Vasco Araujo and Rui Chafes.
facts.excerpt: specially commissioned pieces from Portuguese artists like Vasco Araújo and Rui Chafes

facts.text: Rooms have soundproofed windows that block out the noise of passing trams.
facts.excerpt: Special mention goes to the soundproofed windows, which block out the rumble of the city’s yellow trams as they pass.

facts.text: The fifth-floor restaurant serves Portuguese cuisine created by Chef Bruno Rocha.
facts.excerpt: Go up to the 5th floor and be amazed by the best of Portuguese cuisine, created by Chef Bruno Rocha

facts.text: The ground-floor Patisserie makes Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries in the hotel throughout the day.
facts.excerpt: oﬀers a daily selection of typically Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries freshly made in the hotel throughout the day.

facts.text: The Mezzanine bar on the ground floor serves healthy meals throughout the day.
facts.excerpt: Welcoming and cosy, on a mezzanine on the ground ﬂoor, this bar is the hotel’s meeting point par excellence. You can enjoy our menu of healthy meals throughout the day.

facts.text: A sixth-floor bar is reserved for hotel residents, with views over the rooftops to the River Tagus.
facts.excerpt: only hotel residents can use the sixth-floor bar, a secret spot where blue skies stretch out over the rooftops to the River Tagus

facts.text: The hotel's terrace has a view over the city and the Tejo river.
facts.excerpt: This is the place for those who want to enjoy an incomparable view over the city and the Tejo river.

facts.text: The wellness center has a Susanne Kaufmann spa and a gym.
facts.excerpt: Even with its on-trend Susanne Kaufmann spa, the wellness center, which also includes a gym, still feels like a bit of an afterthought.

facts.text: The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
facts.excerpt: A member of The Leading Hotels of the World, Bairro Alto Hotel is a pioneer

facts.text: The hotel offers guests a guide to Lisbon with off-radar suggestions.
facts.excerpt: There’s also a useful guide to Lisbon with some genuinely off-radar suggestions.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes there are no especially child-friendly corners.
facts.excerpt: Weekending couples and some families from both sides of the Atlantic, although there are no especially child-friendly corners.

facts.text: It is a steep walk down the hill to the banks of the River Tagus.
facts.excerpt: It’s a steep stroll down the hill to the banks of the River Tagus.

facts.text: Tram 28 passes through Chiado near the hotel.
facts.excerpt: Under the watchful eye of Fernando Pessoa, a tram goes by: the "28", as it is known, in operation for more than 100 years.
